o1.biggest_strength: Ranks channels by retained users with the math shown, makes migration a hard launch gate with an undo path and staged rollout, and gives a dated plan with support cover the 3-person team can actually do.
o1.biggest_mistake: Leaves [bracketed placeholders] in the customer-facing X posts and email (speed number, author handles, support address, first name) and pushes Product Hunt to its own day without noting it needs a fresh hook.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Fill every placeholder with real values or a concrete fill-in rule so the X posts and email could be pasted and scheduled today.

o2.biggest_strength: Sharp decision framing: 10% migration-ticket trigger to hold a wave, explicit no-go rule that lets new installs ship without the existing-user update, and a day-4 check with hold rules and a plan B.
o2.biggest_mistake: Moves Product Hunt and Hacker News to 15 December with no reason for the date and loses the 'reach-not-retention' framing, and the email says settings 'carried over on their own' before the staged rollout has actually proven it for most users.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Trigger the existing-user email only when that user's wave has actually shipped and migration is holding, and give one line on why 15 December is the right slot for the reach channels.

reason: Both are strong and on-brief; Output 2 edges it with tighter go/no-go rules, a wave-hold trigger and a plan B I could run without thinking, and its customer copy is cleaner and ready to paste. Output 1's placeholders and its unbounded 'all eight must be true' gate cost it slightly.
